name: Judah and Simeon defeat Adoni-bezek at Bezek
summary: Judah, joined by Simeon, defeats ten thousand Canaanites and Perizzites at Bezek, captures King Adoni-bezek, and cuts off his thumbs and big toes as he had done to seventy other kings.

name: Othniel captures Kiriath-sepher and marries Achsah
summary: Othniel captures Kiriath-sepher to win Caleb's daughter Achsah in marriage, and she persuades her father to give her springs of water along with her inherited land.

name: Israel's tribes fail to drive out the Canaanites
summary: Benjamin, Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan all fail to fully drive out the Canaanites from their territory, instead putting them to forced labor or being pressed back into the hills themselves.

name: The angel of the LORD rebukes Israel at Bochim
summary: An angel confronts Israel for making covenants with Canaan's peoples instead of tearing down their altars, warning that these nations will become thorns and their gods a snare; the people weep and sacrifice at Bochim.

name: Joshua dies and is buried in his inheritance
summary: Joshua dies at a hundred and ten years old and is buried in his own inheritance at Timnath-heres, and the generation that outlives him keeps serving the LORD.

name: A new generation forgets the LORD and the judges cycle begins
summary: A generation grows up not knowing the LORD or what he did for Israel, and a recurring pattern begins: Israel worships Baal, the LORD hands them to oppressors, a judge delivers them, and after the judge dies they fall back into sin.

name: Othniel defeats Cushan-rishathaim and Israel rests forty years
summary: Israel serves the king of Mesopotamia, Cushan-rishathaim, for eight years until the Spirit of the LORD empowers Othniel to defeat him, and the land rests forty years.

name: Ehud assassinates Eglon, the king of Moab
summary: Left-handed Ehud straps a hidden sword to his right thigh, gains a private audience with the obese Eglon by claiming a secret message from God, and kills him in his upper room.

name: Ehud leads Israel to defeat Moab at the Jordan
summary: Ehud sounds a trumpet in the hill country, leads Israel to seize the Jordan's fords, and kills about ten thousand Moabite soldiers, giving the land eighty years of rest.

name: Shamgar kills six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad
summary: Shamgar son of Anath saves Israel by killing six hundred Philistines with a farming tool used to prod oxen.

name: Deborah summons Barak to fight Sisera
summary: Deborah relays the LORD's command for Barak to gather ten thousand men at Mount Tabor, promising to draw Sisera's chariots to the Kishon River; Barak agrees only if Deborah goes with him.

name: The LORD routs Sisera's army at the Kishon River
summary: Barak's army routs Sisera's nine hundred chariots and entire force at the Kishon River, and Sisera abandons his chariot to flee on foot as Barak destroys the rest of his army.

name: Jael kills Sisera with a tent peg
summary: Sisera takes refuge in Jael's tent, and after she gives him milk and covers him to rest, she drives a tent peg through his temple while he sleeps.

name: The song praises Israel's tribes and curses Meroz
summary: Deborah and Barak's victory song praises the tribes who volunteered to fight and pronounces a curse on Meroz for failing to help the LORD against Sisera's army.

name: The song pictures Sisera's mother waiting for his return
summary: The song closes by picturing Sisera's mother watching through a window, reassuring herself that his delay only means the army is still dividing plunder.

name: The angel of the LORD calls Gideon to save Israel
summary: With Israel hiding from Midianite raiders, the angel of the LORD finds Gideon threshing wheat in a winepress and calls him a mighty man of valor sent to save Israel.

name: Gideon tears down his father's altar to Baal
summary: At the LORD's command, Gideon secretly tears down his father's altar to Baal and its Asherah pole by night, builds an altar to the LORD in its place, and is renamed Jerubbaal.

name: Gideon tests the LORD twice with a fleece
summary: Gideon asks for and receives two confirming signs with a wool fleece on the threshing floor, once wet with dew while the ground stays dry and once dry while the ground is wet.

name: The LORD narrows Gideon's army to three hundred
summary: The LORD trims Gideon's army from thirty-two thousand to three hundred, first dismissing the fearful and then choosing only the men who lap water from the spring like a dog.

name: Gideon overhears a Midianite soldier's dream
summary: Gideon sneaks into the edge of the Midianite camp and overhears a soldier's dream of a barley loaf tumbling into camp and flattening a tent, interpreted as Gideon's coming victory.

name: Gideon's three hundred rout Midian's camp
summary: Gideon's three hundred men surround the Midianite camp at night, smash jars to reveal torches, blow trumpets, and shout, throwing the enemy into a panic that turns their own swords against each other.

name: Gideon answers Ephraim's complaint about being excluded
summary: Ephraim's men angrily confront Gideon for not being called to the battle sooner, and he defuses their anger by pointing out that their capture of the Midianite princes outshines his own battle.

name: Succoth and Penuel refuse Gideon's exhausted army bread
summary: Pursuing the Midianite kings, Gideon asks Succoth and Penuel for bread for his weary men; both towns refuse, doubting he will actually capture the kings, and Gideon vows to punish them on his return.

name: Gideon captures and executes Zebah and Zalmunna
summary: Gideon surprises and captures the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna at Karkor, then punishes Succoth and Penuel as promised and executes both kings for killing his brothers at Tabor.

name: Gideon refuses kingship, but his ephod becomes a snare
summary: Gideon refuses Israel's offer to rule over them, declaring that the LORD will rule instead, but the golden ephod he makes from the plunder becomes an object of worship that ensnares his family after his death.

name: Abimelech murders his seventy brothers to become king
summary: With silver from Shechem's temple treasury, Abimelech hires reckless men who murder his seventy half-brothers on one stone at Ophrah; only the youngest, Jotham, escapes, and Shechem makes Abimelech king.

name: Jotham tells the fable of the trees and curses Abimelech
summary: From Mount Gerizim, Jotham tells a fable of trees offering kingship to a worthless bramble, then applies it to Abimelech and Shechem and predicts fire will consume them both.

name: Gaal's revolt leads Abimelech to destroy Shechem
summary: When Gaal incites Shechem to rebel against him, Abimelech ambushes and defeats Gaal's forces, then razes the city itself and burns alive about a thousand people sheltering in its tower.

name: Abimelech dies at Thebez from a millstone
summary: At Thebez, a woman drops an upper millstone on Abimelech's head from a tower, and he orders his armor-bearer to kill him so it will not be said a woman killed him.

name: Tola and Jair judge Israel in succession
summary: Tola of Issachar judges Israel twenty-three years, and after him Jair the Gileadite judges twenty-two years; his thirty sons ride thirty donkeys and control thirty towns called Havvoth-jair.

name: Israel's idolatry brings Ammonite and Philistine oppression
summary: Israel worships the gods of the surrounding nations, and the LORD hands them over to the Philistines and to the Ammonites, who crush Israel east of the Jordan for eighteen years.

name: The LORD relents when Israel puts away its foreign gods
summary: The LORD tells Israel to cry out to the gods they chose instead, but when the people put away their foreign gods and serve him, he can no longer bear their misery.

name: Gilead's elders recruit the outcast Jephthah to lead them
summary: Jephthah, driven out by his half-brothers as the son of a prostitute, is recruited by Gilead's elders to lead them against Ammon after they promise to make him their permanent head.

name: Jephthah's appeal to Ammon's king is rejected
summary: Jephthah sends the king of Ammon a detailed historical argument that Israel never took Ammonite land, but the king ignores the message and prepares for war.

name: Jephthah vows to sacrifice whatever meets him at his door
summary: Before battle, Jephthah vows that if the LORD gives him victory, he will offer up as a burnt offering whatever comes out of his house to meet him on his return.

name: Jephthah defeats Ammon and sacrifices his daughter
summary: Jephthah devastates twenty Ammonite towns and wins the war, but his only daughter is the first to come out to meet him, and after two months to mourn, he fulfills his vow.

name: Ephraim threatens Jephthah for not being called to battle
summary: Ephraim's men confront Jephthah, angry at being excluded from the fight against Ammon and threatening to burn down his house.

name: Gilead defeats Ephraim and catches survivors with Shibboleth
summary: Jephthah's men defeat Ephraim and seize the Jordan's fords, catching fleeing Ephraimites by making them say Shibboleth, a word their dialect could not pronounce correctly.

name: Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon judge Israel in succession
summary: Ibzan of Bethlehem, Elon the Zebulunite, and Abdon son of Hillel each judge Israel in turn, together covering twenty-five years before the next oppression begins.

name: An angel announces Samson's birth to Manoah's wife
summary: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah's barren wife she will bear a son who must never drink wine, eat anything unclean, or have his hair cut, since he will be a Nazirite who begins delivering Israel from the Philistines.

name: Manoah offers a sacrifice and the angel ascends in its flame
summary: Manoah offers a burnt offering on a rock, and the angel of the LORD ascends to heaven in its flame, leaving Manoah and his wife afraid until she reasons the LORD would not have accepted their offering if he meant to kill them.

name: Samson is born and the Spirit begins to stir him
summary: Manoah's wife bears a son named Samson, and as he grows the Spirit of the LORD begins to stir him in the camp between Zorah and Eshtaol.

name: Samson insists on marrying a Philistine woman from Timnah
summary: Samson tells his reluctant parents to get him a Philistine woman from Timnah as his wife, insisting she is right in his own eyes.

name: Samson kills a lion and later eats honey from its carcass
summary: The Spirit of the LORD empowers Samson to tear apart a young lion with his bare hands, and on a later trip he scrapes honey from bees that have nested in its carcass, sharing it without saying where it came from.

name: Samson's riddle wager is betrayed at his wedding feast
summary: Samson wagers thirty garments on a riddle about the lion and the honey, and after his wife weeps and pries out the answer, he pays the debt by killing thirty Philistines at Ashkelon.

name: Samson burns Philistine fields with three hundred foxes
summary: After learning his wife has been given to his best man, Samson catches three hundred foxes, ties torches between their tails in pairs, and sends them through the Philistines' grain fields, olive orchards, and shocks.

name: Samson strikes down the Philistines who killed his wife
summary: The Philistines burn Samson's wife and father-in-law to death for the fox fires, and Samson strikes them with a great blow in revenge before retreating to a cave.

name: Samson kills a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone
summary: After Judah's men hand Samson over to keep the peace, the Spirit of the LORD rushes on him, his ropes fall away, and he kills a thousand Philistines with a fresh donkey's jawbone.

name: The LORD provides water for the thirsty Samson at Lehi
summary: Exhausted and desperately thirsty after the battle, Samson cries out to the LORD, who splits open a hollow place at Lehi and produces water that revives him.

name: Samson tears down Gaza's city gate
summary: Trapped in Gaza overnight by an ambush at the city gate, Samson rises at midnight, tears the gate's doors and posts out of the ground, and carries them to a hill near Hebron.

name: Delilah's first three attempts to learn Samson's secret fail
summary: Paid by the Philistine lords, Delilah presses Samson three times for the secret of his strength, but his answers about fresh bowstrings, new ropes, and a woven loom all prove false.

name: Samson reveals his Nazirite secret and loses his strength
summary: Worn down by Delilah's daily pressure, Samson finally tells her his strength depends on his uncut Nazirite hair, and after he falls asleep on her lap she has it shaved off, and his strength leaves him.

name: Samson pulls down the temple of Dagon in his death
summary: Blinded and bound in Gaza, Samson prays for strength one last time, pushes apart the two central pillars of the Philistines' temple, and kills more Philistines in his death than in his life.

name: Micah's mother dedicates stolen silver to make idols
summary: Micah confesses to stealing eleven hundred pieces of silver from his mother, who dedicates it to the LORD and uses part of it to have a carved and a metal image made for his shrine.

name: A wandering Levite becomes Micah's household priest
summary: A young Levite from Bethlehem looking for a place to live agrees to serve as Micah's priest for silver, clothing, and food, and Micah assumes the LORD will now prosper him.

name: Danite spies find Micah's shrine and its promising priest
summary: Five Danite spies looking for land lodge at Micah's house, recognize his priest, and ask him to inquire of God, receiving assurance that their journey is under the LORD's eye.

name: Six hundred armed Danites take Micah's idols and his priest
summary: Six hundred armed Danites take Micah's carved image, ephod, and household gods, and persuade his priest to come with them by offering him a whole tribe to serve instead of one household; Micah can only protest before turning back.

name: The Danites conquer Laish and rename it Dan
summary: The Danites attack the quiet, undefended city of Laish, burn it, rebuild it as their own, rename it Dan, and set up Micah's carved image for their tribe to worship.

name: The Levite retrieves his concubine from Bethlehem
summary: A Levite travels to Bethlehem to persuade his concubine to return with him, and after her father delays their departure for days, they finally set out late in the day toward home.

name: The men of Gibeah abuse the Levite's concubine through the night
summary: Lodging in Gibeah, the Levite's host is confronted by the town's men demanding to abuse his guest; they instead seize the concubine and abuse her through the night, and she dies by morning.

name: The Levite sends his concubine's body throughout Israel
summary: The Levite finds his concubine's body at the doorway, carries her home, and cuts her into twelve pieces to send to each tribe of Israel, provoking universal shock.

name: Israel assembles at Mizpah to hear the Levite's account
summary: Israel's tribes gather as one at Mizpah, and the Levite recounts what Gibeah's men did to his concubine, prompting a demand that Benjamin hand over the guilty men.

name: Benjamin's refusal costs Israel two early battles
summary: Benjamin refuses to surrender the men of Gibeah and musters twenty-six thousand swordsmen plus seven hundred more from Gibeah, among them elite left-handed slingers, defeating Israel's larger army in two separate battles.

name: Israel ambushes Gibeah and nearly destroys Benjamin
summary: Using a hidden ambush and a burning city as a signal, Israel finally routs Benjamin's army, leaving only six hundred men alive after also destroying Benjamin's other towns.

name: Israel weeps at Bethel over Benjamin's near-destruction
summary: Realizing their oath at Mizpah bars them from giving Benjamin wives and that a tribe of Israel now faces extinction, the people gather at Bethel to weep and offer sacrifices.

name: Israel destroys Jabesh-gilead and spares its virgins for Benjamin
summary: Israel discovers that Jabesh-gilead sent no one to the assembly at Mizpah, sends twelve thousand men to destroy the city, and gives its four hundred surviving virgins to the men of Benjamin as wives.

name: Benjamin's remaining men seize wives from Shiloh's dancers
summary: Since Jabesh-gilead's women are not enough, Israel's elders let Benjamin's remaining men hide in the vineyards at Shiloh's yearly festival and seize wives from among the dancing daughters of the town.
